issue: Pragmatics: a cashier never addresses a customer as 'kamu' — counter speech uses Kak/Bu/Pak or just 'Totalnya...'. 'Total belanjaan kamu' from staff reads impolite and unreal.

fix.target: Totalnya enam ratus sembilan puluh ribu rupiah, Kak.
fix.english: The total is six hundred and ninety thousand rupiah, miss.

issue: Calque: 'masih terlalu mahal untuk saya' mirrors English 'still too expensive for me'. The bargaining idiom at the stall is 'masih mahal' / 'kemahalan'.

fix.target: Wah, masih kemahalan, Pak.
fix.english: Wow, that is still way too expensive, sir.
fix.grammar: ke-...-an makes 'too X': mahal → kemahalan = too expensive, overpriced.

issue: Seller addressing a customer as 'kamu' is impolite/unreal — the giving-in formula is 'Ya sudah, khusus buat Ibu/Kakak'. 'Baiklah' is also stiff for market talk.

fix.target: Ya sudah, khusus untuk Ibu, dua ratus ribu saja.
fix.english: Alright then, just for you, ma'am, only two hundred thousand.
fix.grammar: Ya sudah = alright then — the giving-in phrase: Ya sudah, dua ratus ribu saja.

issue: Factually off and wrong verb: at an ATM you cover the KEYPAD (tombol), not the screen, and covering = tutupi; 'tutup layar' reads as 'close/shut the screen'.

fix.target: Tutupi tombol dengan tangan waktu memasukkan PIN.
fix.english: Cover the keypad with your hand when entering your PIN.

issue: Spelling: KBBI standard is 'prangko'; 'perangko' is a widespread but nonstandard variant — a deck should model the standard form.

fix.target: Saya membeli prangko untuk mengirim kartu pos ke teman.
fix.english: I bought stamps to send a postcard to a friend.

issue: For packages the everyday verb is 'sampai' — the plaintive idiom is 'belum sampai juga'. 'belum tiba juga' pairs a formal verb with a colloquial complaint pattern.

fix.target: Paket dari ibu saya belum sampai juga.
fix.english: The package from my mother still has not arrived.

issue: Nonstandard double object: 'meminjamkan saya uang' — the -kan verb takes the THING as object (meminjamkan uang ke saya); the deck's own id-1524 models the correct pattern. Tip repeats the flawed frame.

fix.target: Kakak meminjamkan uang ke saya untuk membeli buku kuliah.
fix.english: My older sibling lent me money to buy college books.
fix.grammar: meminjam = borrow, meminjamkan = lend: meminjamkan uang ke saya = lent money to me.

issue: '...atau tidak' makes the cashier's offer blunt ('or not?'). The real checkout formula is simply 'Struknya mau dibawa, Kak?'

fix.target: Struknya mau dibawa, Kak?
fix.english: Would you like the receipt, miss?

issue: Nobody heading out to change money says 'tempat penukaran uang' — the universal spoken term is the loan 'money changer'; the long form lives on signage. Deck already uses loans (QRIS, transfer).

fix.target: Saya menukar dolar di money changer dekat hotel.
fix.english: I exchange dollars at the money changer near the hotel.
fix.grammar: Indonesians say money changer; tempat penukaran uang is the formal sign version.

issue: Register realism: office speech overwhelmingly uses the loan 'deadline'; 'tenggat' is journalistic/formal writing. Six cards (1444/45/49/52/54/55) model tenggat as the default spoken word — keep at most one as the formal synonym.

fix.target: Deadline laporan ini hari Kamis jam lima sore.
fix.english: The deadline for this report is Thursday at five in the afternoon.
fix.grammar: Office speech uses deadline; tenggat is its formal written synonym.

issue: Same tenggat-as-everyday-speech issue as id-1444: spoken office Indonesian says 'sebelum deadline'.

fix.target: Saya harus menyelesaikan revisi ini sebelum deadline.
fix.english: I have to finish this revision before the deadline.

issue: 'mengejar tenggat' is a bookish rendering of the ubiquitous office idiom 'kejar deadline' — no one races a 'tenggat' out loud.

fix.target: Tim kami sedang mengejar deadline proyek minggu ini.
fix.english: Our team is chasing the project deadline this week.
fix.grammar: kejar deadline = race the deadline: kami sedang mengejar deadline.

issue: Same tenggat register issue; spoken form is 'deadline-nya besok'. The -nya tip itself is good and transfers cleanly.

fix.target: Deadline-nya besok, tapi laporan saya sudah selesai hari ini.
fix.english: The deadline is tomorrow, but my report is already finished today.
fix.grammar: -nya can mean 'the one we know': deadline-nya besok = the deadline is tomorrow.

issue: Same tenggat register issue: 'supaya selesai sebelum deadline' is what a teammate would actually say.

fix.target: Ayo kita bagi tugas supaya selesai sebelum deadline.
fix.english: Let's divide the tasks so we finish before the deadline.

issue: Same tenggat register issue; the tinggal tip is fine and unaffected.

fix.target: Waktu kita tinggal dua hari sebelum deadline proyek.
fix.english: We only have two days left before the project deadline.

issue: 'mengumpulkan laporan' is school hand-in language and also parses as 'collecting reports (from others)'. Office speech for submitting on time is mengirim/menyerahkan laporan.

fix.target: Dia selalu mengirim laporan tepat waktu.
fix.english: He always sends in his reports on time.

issue: The idiom is reduplicated: 'jauh-jauh hari' = well in advance. Clipped 'dari jauh hari' occurs in print but sounds off in speech.

fix.target: Kalau mau cuti panjang, ajukan jauh-jauh hari.
fix.english: If you want a long leave, put in for it well in advance.
fix.grammar: jauh-jauh hari = well in advance: ajukan jauh-jauh hari.

issue: 'pada hari Jumat' is paper bureaucratese in a spoken request — even a formal request to Pak Dedi drops 'pada'. Policy: formal cards must read natural, not stilted.

fix.target: Pak Dedi, saya mohon izin cuti hari Jumat.
fix.english: Mr. Dedi, I would like to request leave on Friday.

issue: Register clash: formal 'permohonan ... disetujui' glued to casual 'kamu'. HR speech says 'pengajuan cuti', matching mengajukan taught in id-1462.

fix.target: Pengajuan cuti kamu sudah disetujui atasan.
fix.english: Your leave request has been approved by the boss.

issue: 'rekan tim' is a clipped calque of 'teammate' — natural Indonesian is 'teman satu tim' or 'rekan kerja'.

fix.target: Selama saya sakit, tugas saya dikerjakan teman satu tim.
fix.english: While I was sick, my tasks were done by a teammate.

issue: Interview register: this is the interviewer speaking, and interviews are formal (policy rule 4) — interviewers use Anda, not kamu, and say 'perusahaan sebelumnya', not 'perusahaan lama'.

fix.target: Ceritakan pengalaman kerja Anda di perusahaan sebelumnya.
fix.english: Tell me about your work experience at your previous company.
fix.grammar: Interviewers use Anda, never kamu: pengalaman kerja Anda = your work experience.

issue: 'Email saya penuh' says the mailbox is out of storage; the after-leave situation is a backlog — the idiom is 'email menumpuk' (piled up). The gloss carries the same calque.

fix.target: Email saya menumpuk setelah cuti seminggu.
fix.english: My emails piled up after a week of leave.
fix.grammar: menumpuk = to pile up: email menumpuk = emails piled up.
